aisBaselineNote: transitsBaseline is withheld (null) until 72 hourly samples exist on the active30m basis, roughly 3 days after the 2026-07-20 cutover, and is published once that gate is met. Pre-cutover samples used a different counting basis and are not mixed in. It is an AIS concurrent-presence median, a different population from transits.baseline (IMF PortWatch daily crossings); do not divide one by the other.

carrierSuspensions.notes: Mediterranean Shipping Company is routing all Asia–Europe vessels via the Cape of Good Hope; Gulf calls limited to escorted convoys.
A.P. Moller–Maersk has suspended new Strait of Hormuz transits and is rerouting Gulf-bound cargo via Jebel Ali transhipment with Cape diversions for Asia–Europe.
CMA CGM has activated Cape of Good Hope routing for all Asia–Europe services; spot rates up roughly 60% on affected lanes.
COSCO Shipping continues selective Gulf transits under convoy escort but has suspended bookings to Bandar Abbas; Cape rerouting in effect for Europe-bound.
Hapag-Lloyd has suspended Hormuz transits and is rerouting via the Cape; surcharges layered on top of existing Red Sea contingency adders.
Ocean Network Express is routing Asia–Europe via the Cape; Gulf service suspended pending convoy availability.
Evergreen Marine is diverting Asia–Europe loops via the Cape and has paused new Gulf bookings.
HMM has implemented Cape rerouting for Asia–Europe and is operating limited Gulf service through alliance partners.
Yang Ming Marine Transport has shifted Asia–Europe services to the Cape route in coordination with THE Alliance partners.

chokepointsNote: preCrisisBaselineMedian on every row is computed over one fixed window (baselineWindowStart to baselineWindowEnd) anchored to the Hormuz crisis. For hormuz that window is a genuine pre-crisis baseline. For bab-el-mandeb, suez and cape it is not: those routes were already carrying diverted Red Sea traffic within that window, so preCrisisBaselineMedian for those rows reads as wartime volume, not a peacetime figure.

bullets: BREAKING: London insurers widened the Red Sea high-risk zone following Houthi attacks, per gCaptain; not independently confirmed by a second source.
Qatar sent its first LNG shipment through the Strait of Hormuz in three weeks, per gCaptain, as IRGC-US exchange of strikes continues across the region.
Crisis Pressure sits in the extreme band; Escalation Forecast is in the elevated band, with Polymarket escalation contracts the top forecast driver.
dailyBrief.summary: The Strait of Hormuz remains under acute operational pressure. Port arrivals across the Hormuz-area ports on both the Persian Gulf and Gulf of Oman sides reached 637 vessels in the most recent 24 hours, while PortWatch's most recent published day (2026-07-23) recorded 10 transits against a pre-crisis baseline of 88 per day; the two figures use different methodologies and should not be compared directly. At 14:52 UTC, 339 vessels were anchored or stopped in the region, and 29 indexed events were recorded in the last 24 hours. Brent crude stood at $89.73 at 14:52 UTC, down 0.12% over the prior 24 hours. The site's composite Crisis Pressure index is in the extreme band, with physical transit deviation the leading contributor; the Escalation Forecast index, a horizon-mix composite, sits in the elevated band, driven primarily by Polymarket escalation contracts. The two indices diverge: current pressure is more severe than the forward-looking signal. Iranian state media (IRNA, Mehr News) claim IRGC ballistic missiles destroyed three US F-35 jets at Al-Azraq Air Base in Jordan and struck Ali Al Salem Air Base in Kuwait; these claims are not independently confirmed. Per gCaptain, Qatar resumed LNG exports through the strait for the first time in over three weeks. London insurers widened the Red Sea high-risk zone following Houthi attacks, per gCaptain, though this report has not been independently confirmed.

pipelineBypass.name: Petroline (East-West Pipeline)
pipelineBypass.notes: Saudi Aramco's East-West Pipeline carries Arabian Light from Abqaiq to Yanbu on the Red Sea, the single largest non-Hormuz route for Gulf crude.

pipelineBypass.name: ADCOP (Habshan-Fujairah)
pipelineBypass.notes: ADNOC's Habshan-Fujairah pipeline lifts UAE crude past the Strait of Hormuz to Fujairah on the Gulf of Oman, where it loads on tankers transiting the open Indian Ocean.

pipelineBypass.name: Goreh-Jask Pipeline
pipelineBypass.notes: Iran's pipeline from the southwest oilfields to Jask on the Gulf of Oman bypasses the Strait, but throughput remains a fraction of nameplate capacity.
